explore_prose: Every run in this experiment is in the explorer below: filter by outcome to see which settings held the SLOs, or by setting to compare one sweep against another.
Each sweep's hypothesis was written before the runs, and is quoted beside that sweep's measured result below.

hero.html: 776 configurations over 11 sweeps (pipeline-batch, dp-batch, moe-collective, eplb, kv-capacity-pipeline, kv-capacity-dp, cudagraph-pipeline, cudagraph-dp, expert-parallel, disaggregated, pd-threshold), each at 5 load levels, every run on exactly 16 GPUs.
1x TP8xDP2 + EP (max seqs 512), from the moe-collective sweep, reached 393.16 tok/s/accelerator (6290.5 tok/s across the fleet) at concurrency 512 while holding the scenario's SLOs.
1x TP8xDP2 + EP (max seqs 512) at concurrency 512. 1950 of 3880 runs held the SLOs.

recommendation_prose: The table below ranks the measured operating points by output tok/s per accelerator, the objective this experiment selects on, among runs that held the scenario's SLOs.

prose: Pipeline stages only pay once the batch cap is high enough to keep every stage busy, so pp should lose least at large max_num_seqs.
Measured: best was 1x TP16 + EP (max seqs 256) at 245.53 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 256).
sections.title: Sweep: pipeline-batch

prose: Data-parallel attention splits the batch across ranks, so the batch caps should bind later at tp4 dp4 than at tp8 dp2.
Measured: best was 1x TP8xDP2 + EP (max seqs 256) at 283.77 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 256).
sections.title: Sweep: dp-batch

prose: DeepEP backends should cost more as dp widens, and low-latency should fit only at small step budgets.
Measured: best was 1x TP8xDP2 + EP (max seqs 512) at 393.16 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 512).
sections.title: Sweep: moe-collective

prose: Redundant experts should cost a little memory and buy nothing on uniform synthetic routing.
Measured: best was 1x TP8xDP2 + EP at 283.77 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 256).
sections.title: Sweep: eplb

prose: Narrower tensor groups hold more weight per rank, so KV headroom should bind on 2-instance and deep-pp shapes, not on tp16.
Measured: best was 2x TP8 + EP (gpu mem util 0.95 · KV dtype fp8) at 266.72 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 256).
sections.title: Sweep: kv-capacity-pipeline

prose: Data-parallel ranks each replicate attention weights, so fp8 KV and memory utilization should matter more at tp4 dp4.
Measured: best was 1x TP8xDP2 + EP (KV dtype fp8) at 286.17 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 256).
sections.title: Sweep: kv-capacity-dp

prose: Full graph capture should cut per-step launch cost on every cut, but only where the memory it reserves still fits.
Measured: best was 2x TP8 + EP (gpu mem util 0.95 · graph capture full+piecewise) at 264.94 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 256).
sections.title: Sweep: cudagraph-pipeline

prose: Graph capture should help the data-parallel shapes as much as the tensor-parallel ones, memory permitting.
Measured: best was 1x TP8xDP2 + EP (gpu mem util 0.95 · graph capture full) at 284.83 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 256).
sections.title: Sweep: cudagraph-dp

prose: Sharding experts should beat replicating them at tp16, and matter less once pipeline stages already split the weights.
Measured: best was 1x TP16 + EP (max seqs 256) at 245.53 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 256).
sections.title: Sweep: expert-parallel

prose: Splitting prefill from decode should help little on short chatbot prompts, since the KV handoff costs more than the interference it removes.
Measured: best was 1P/1D TP8 + EP (max seqs 256) at 126.11 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 128).
sections.title: Sweep: disaggregated

prose: Disaggregating only prompts above a few hundred tokens should keep short turns local and beat always-split.
Measured: best was 1P/1D TP8 + EP at 63.35 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 512).
sections.title: Sweep: pd-threshold
